title: Strong Collocations
intro: Heavy rain, not strong rain. Deeply sorry, not very sorry. English pairs its intensifiers with fixed partners — match the pair that actually exists.

A2.why: Make a big mistake, never “do a big mistake”: Spanish “hacer” is the trap.
Rain is heavy, not strong: “lluvia fuerte” becomes “heavy rain”.

A2.right: coffee with a lot of flavour
A2.why: Coffee and tea are strong or weak, never “heavy” or “hard”.
“Fast” here means firmly, not quickly: someone fast asleep won’t wake easily.
Wide awake is the opposite of fast asleep: eyes wide open.
Sleep is deep or light, like water: a deep sleep is hard to wake from.

A2.right: work that needs a lot of effort
A2.why: “Hard work” is the fixed pair; “trabajo duro” translates neatly for once.
A clever idea is bright, like a light switching on in your head.
Smokers and drinkers are heavy, never “strong”.
Wind is strong, but rain is heavy: don’t swap them.

A2.right: a lot of money to pay
A2.why: Prices are high or low, never “expensive”: the thing is expensive, its price is high.

A2.right: a cold that makes you feel really ill
A2.why: A cold is bad or heavy, not “strong”: “un resfriado fuerte” is a bad cold.

B1.right: a large number of vehicles on the road
B1.why: Traffic is heavy or light, never “strong”.
Smells and tastes are strong, unlike rain, which is heavy.

B1.right: a strong feeling of sadness about something
B1.why: Deep feelings take “deep”: deep regret, deep sadness, deep respect.
A range is wide, like a long shelf full of choices.
Hopes are high, like expectations: “We have high hopes for the new doctor.”
Friends are close, not “near”: it is about the relationship, not distance.
“It’s a great pleasure to meet you” is a fixed polite phrase.
People are badly injured, things are badly damaged.

B1.right: a long breath that fills your lungs
B1.why: Take a deep breath, not “a big breath”: the air goes deep down.

B1.right: a way of speaking that clearly shows where you are from
B1.why: Accents are strong or slight: “He has a strong Valencian accent.”

B1.right: a fever: your body is much hotter than normal
B1.why: Doctors say “a high temperature” for a fever, not “a big fever”.
“Bitterly” pairs with cold: the kind of cold that bites.

B2.why: Formal apologies use “deeply”: “We are deeply sorry for the delay.”
Disappointment is bitter, like a sour taste that stays in your mouth.
“Utterly” goes with extreme adjectives like exhausted, not with plain “tired”.
“Highly” pairs with likely and unlikely, never with big or tall.
Often a firm phrase: “I want to make this perfectly clear.”

B2.right: known by a great many people
B2.why: “Widely” means spread among many people: widely known, widely used.
Things are severely damaged: “The stagecoach was severely damaged in the crash.”
“Fully aware” stresses you know it all: “I’m fully aware of the risks.”

B2.right: praised and suggested by many people
B2.why: “Highly” again: a highly recommended restaurant gets praise from many people.
The outlaws were heavily armed: “heavily” means carrying a large amount.

B2.right: so unwell that it is dangerous
B2.why: People are seriously ill, never “strongly ill” or “heavily ill”.
“Closely” goes with linked and related: smoking is closely linked to lung disease.

C1.why: Furious is already extreme, so it takes “absolutely”, not “very”.
“Blatantly” means openly, without shame: blatantly unfair, blatantly obvious.
You know it so clearly that it hurts a little.
“Profoundly” is a formal, deep intensifier: profoundly grateful, profoundly moved.

C1.right: very noticeably clear, almost embarrassingly so
C1.why: Glaring like a harsh light: impossible not to see.

C1.right: extremely favourable, by a large margin
C1.why: Reviews or votes are overwhelmingly positive when nearly everyone agrees.
“Staunch” means loyal and firm: a staunch opponent never changes sides.

C1.right: sharply and intensely ashamed in front of others
C1.why: “Acutely” means sharply: acutely embarrassed, acutely aware, acute pain.
“Eminently” means highly, mostly with sensible, suitable and reasonable.

C1.right: far, far better than the rest
C1.why: “Vastly” means by a huge amount: vastly superior, vastly different.

C1.right: firmly fixed and very hard to change
C1.why: Entrenched like soldiers in a trench: beliefs and habits that won’t move.
“Fiercely” suits strong feelings: fiercely independent, fiercely loyal.
